items.name: Apache86 (QTS 6 / Hero6) (Release Candidate 4 Preview)
items.description:
Apache86 is a complete modern Web hosting platform for QNAP NAS running QTS 6 or QuTS hero 6. It provides a self-contained Apache HTTP Server environment with PHP 8.6, PHP-FPM, TLS management, virtual hosts, security tools, diagnostics, application integration and a dedicated Web administration interface. Apache86 can be used both as a traditional Web server and as a common Web runtime for other QPKG applications.

Main features

  • Apache HTTP Server
  • PHP 8.6 with PHP-FPM
  • HTTP and HTTPS hosting
  • Virtual host management
  • Apache module manager
  • PHP extension manager
  • PHP-FPM pool management
  • OPcache and PHP performance information
  • Authenticated phpinfo() based on the private PHP-FPM FastCGI listener
  • TLS certificate management
  • Self-signed certificate support
  • QTS certificate import
  • Let's Encrypt / ACME support
  • ModSecurity Web Application Firewall integration
  • Reverse proxy support
  • Load-balancer support
  • Python / WSGI support
  • Python virtual environments
  • Hosted Applications registry for dependent QPKGs
  • Runtime diagnostics
  • Security audit
  • Configuration snapshots
  • Transactional validation and rollback
  • Detailed Apache, PHP and application logs
  • Responsive dark Web interface
  • 20 interface languages
  • x86_64 and ARM64 support

Hosted Applications

Apache86 can act as the shared Web runtime for other QPKG packages. Dependent QPKGs can declare their own:
  • DocumentRoot
  • Apache modules
  • PHP extensions
  • PHP-FPM pool
  • Virtual Host
  • backend service
  • health check
through an Apache86 application manifest. Application files remain inside the dependent QPKG. They are not copied into the Apache86 Web directory. This allows Apache86 and hosted applications to be installed, upgraded or removed independently. The Apache86 interface can show which applications depend on specific Apache modules or PHP extensions and warn before a required component is disabled.

Included PHP extensions

The core PHP build includes: bcmath, bz2, calendar, ctype, curl, date, dba, dom, exif, FFI, fileinfo, filter, ftp, gd, gettext, gmp, hash, iconv, intl, json, ldap, libxml, mbstring, mysqli, mysqlnd, odbc, openssl, pcntl, pcre, PDO, pdo_dblib, pdo_mysql, pdo_odbc, pdo_pgsql, pdo_sqlite, pgsql, Phar, posix, random, readline, Reflection, session, shmop, SimpleXML, snmp, soap, sockets, sodium, SPL, sqlite3, standard, sysvmsg, sysvsem, sysvshm, tidy, tokenizer, uri, xml, xmlreader, xmlwriter, xsl, zip and Zend OPcache.

Additional PECL extensions

Apache86 also attempts to build and validate a large set of optional PHP extensions: pspell, igbinary, msgpack, apcu, redis, memcached, memcache, mongodb, gnupg, yaml, ssh2, mailparse, timezonedb, oauth, ds, protobuf, ast, uuid, inotify, uploadprogress, excimer, lzf, zstd, simdjson, decimal, json_post, pcov, xdebug, amqp, rdkafka, event, ev, gearman, maxminddb, swoole, grpc, opentelemetry, raphf, http, xlswriter, csv, stats, trader, xattr, krb5, radius, hrtime and scrypt. Additional conditional extensions include:
  • imap
  • imagick
  • oci8
  • pdo_oci
  • sqlsrv
  • pdo_sqlsrv
depending on source compatibility and the availability of their required external libraries or client SDKs. Xdebug and PCOV are installed disabled by default to avoid unnecessary runtime overhead. Because PECL compatibility can change between PHP versions and architectures, Apache86 generates an exact extension inventory during the build so the installed package can report which optional modules were successfully built and loaded.

Database connectivity

Apache86 includes support for:
  • MySQL / MariaDB
  • PostgreSQL
  • SQLite
  • ODBC
  • FreeTDS / Microsoft SQL compatible connections
  • Oracle when Oracle Instant Client is available
  • Microsoft SQL Server native PHP drivers when Microsoft ODBC Driver is available
  • MongoDB through PECL

Security

Apache86 includes:
  • authenticated management interface
  • CSRF protection
  • secure management sessions
  • TLS support
  • ModSecurity integration
  • configuration validation before reload
  • transactional configuration updates
  • automatic rollback
  • module dependency protection
  • Hosted Application manifest validation
  • path validation
  • health checks
  • security diagnostics
  • detailed audit logs
Sensitive diagnostic pages such as phpinfo() are accessible only after management authentication and are not exposed as public PHP files.

Default ports

  • HTTP: 18080
  • HTTPS: 18443
  • Management UI: 12408
  • PHP-FPM FastCGI: 127.0.0.1:19086
The private PHP-FPM endpoint is not exposed to the network.

Requirements

  • QNAP QTS 6 or later
  • QuTS hero 6 or later
  • x86_64 or ARM64 NAS

Typical uses

Apache86 is suitable for:
  • PHP Web applications
  • CMS platforms
  • private cloud applications
  • custom QPKG Web interfaces
  • reverse proxies
  • Python WSGI applications
  • development environments
  • self-hosted services
  • shared Web infrastructure for multiple QPKGs

Quick start

After installation, open the Apache86 management interface and authenticate using the credentials generated during initial setup. You can then:
  1. create or import a Virtual Host,
  2. configure PHP and PHP-FPM,
  3. enable the required modules and extensions,
  4. configure HTTPS,
  5. deploy your Web application,
  6. verify it using Diagnostics, Audit and Logs.
Apache86 preserves user configuration across package upgrades and validates configuration changes before applying them.

items.name: Unifi-toolkit (Apache85)
items.description:
UniFi Toolkit by Crosstalk Solutions is an open-source network monitoring and management suite for Ubiquiti UniFi environments.

This native QNAP edition runs directly on your NAS using Python from Apache85, without Docker, Container Station, or additional services.
Main Features
  • Dashboard: Real-time gateway status, CPU, memory, WAN connections, VPN status, and connected clients.
  • Network Pulse: Live network statistics, access point monitoring, and bandwidth visualization.
  • Wi-Fi Stalker: Track wired and wireless clients, roaming history, signal strength, and device activity.
  • Threat Watch: Monitor IDS/IPS security events, analyze threats, and configure webhook notifications.
  • House Arrest: Isolate devices, restrict Internet access, and manage network firewall policies.
  • Security: HTTPS access, password-protected administration, encrypted credentials, and SQLite database storage.
Compatibility & Requirements
  • QTS 5 / QuTS hero 5 or newer
  • x86_64 and ARM64 (aarch64)
  • Required QPKG dependency: Apache85 only
  • Python runtime provided by Apache85
  • UniFi OS console (UDM, UCG, Cloud Key Gen2+, etc.)
  • UniFi Network 9.0+ required for House Arrest firewall features
No Docker or FFmpeg required.
Web Interface
After installation, open: https://YOUR-NAS-IP:17889 HTTPS is enabled by default. Your browser may display a certificate warning because the initial certificate is self-signed.
IMPORTANT – Default Username and Password
Default username: admin The administrator password is generated randomly during the first startup. Method 1 – QTS Event Log (Recommended)
  1. Log in to your QNAP NAS administration interface.
  2. Open QuLog Center.
  3. Navigate to Local Device → Event Log.
  4. Search for UniFi Toolkit.
  5. Locate the event containing the administrator username and generated password.
The credentials are recorded automatically in the QTS Event Log after the first successful startup. Method 2 – SSH Access If the event is unavailable, connect to your NAS via SSH and execute: cat /opt/Unifi-ToolKit/etc/initial-password.txt This file contains the administrator username and password. Forgot Your Password? Connect via SSH and execute: /opt/Unifi-ToolKit/reset-password.sh A new random password will be generated and recorded in the QTS Event Log. The local password file will also be updated. Security note: Passwords recorded in QTS events are visible to authorized log viewers. Change your password after the initial login and protect access to NAS logs.
Updates & Persistent Configuration
Application updates preserve your existing configuration, UniFi controller settings, encryption keys, SSL certificates, and SQLite database. Built-in service management scripts provide start, stop, restart, status, and password reset operations. Installation directory: /opt/Unifi-ToolKit Default HTTPS port: 17889 Source code: https://github.com/Crosstalk-Solutions/unifi-toolkit Original project: Crosstalk Solutions

items.name: CUPS

Turn your QNAP NAS into a network print server to manage, share and monitor printers through a secure HTTPS web interface.

Useful Information

To retrieve your administrator password via SSH: cat /opt/CUPS/etc/cups/.cupsadmin-password A browser certificate warning may appear because CUPS uses a self-signed HTTPS certificate by default.

items.name: Unifi Network Optimizer (Apache85)
items.description:
NetworkOptimizer is a powerful, self-hosted network monitoring, optimization and security auditing solution designed for Ubiquiti UniFi environments.

This native QNAP package runs directly on QTS 6 and QuTS hero 6 without Docker, providing a centralized web interface to monitor network performance, analyze Wi-Fi quality, identify security risks and optimize UniFi configurations.

Key Features

  • UniFi Network Monitoring: Monitor network devices, clients, connectivity and overall network health.
  • Wi-Fi Optimization: Analyze wireless performance, channel utilization, interference and configuration.
  • Security Auditing: Identify potential vulnerabilities, firewall issues and network configuration weaknesses.
  • Configuration Optimization: Receive recommendations to improve UniFi network performance and security.
  • Speed Testing: WAN and LAN performance testing with iperf3 integration.
  • Adaptive SQM: Advanced traffic management and bufferbloat optimization.
  • Alerts & Scheduling: Automated network checks, monitoring and notifications.
  • Multi-Site Management: Centralized visibility across multiple UniFi sites.
  • Persistent Configuration: Application settings, credentials and databases are preserved during package updates.

Requirements

  • QTS 6.x or QuTS hero 6.x
  • x86_64 or ARM64 NAS
  • Apache85 QPKG dependency (provides ICU libraries)
  • Minimum 2 GB RAM recommended
  • Network connectivity to a UniFi Controller
The application uses a self-contained .NET 10 runtime. No Docker, external Python runtime or separate .NET installation is required.

Quick Start

1. Installation Install Apache85 first, then install the NetworkOptimizer QPKG package. 2. Access the Web Interface Open your browser and navigate to: http://YOUR_NAS_IP:8042 3. Initial Login Default username: admin The administrator password is automatically generated during the first startup. Find it in the QNAP system event logs (when available) or inspect the application log via SSH: 
grep -i -A5 'AUTO-GENERATED' /opt/NetworkOptimizer/logs/runtime.log
4. Connect Your UniFi Controller Open Settings in NetworkOptimizer, enter your UniFi Controller URL and configure a dedicated local UniFi account with the required permissions. Ubiquiti cloud SSO credentials are not supported for this connection. 5. Start Monitoring Open the Audit dashboard to perform your first network security assessment. Explore Wi-Fi Optimizer, network monitoring and speed-testing features. Some advanced operations require SSH access to your UniFi gateway or devices.

Service Management

/opt/NetworkOptimizer/start.sh
/opt/NetworkOptimizer/stop.sh
/opt/NetworkOptimizer/restart.sh
/opt/NetworkOptimizer/status.sh
/opt/NetworkOptimizer/healthcheck.sh
Default Web Port: 8042 (HTTP) Installation Directory: /opt/NetworkOptimizer Runtime Logs: /opt/NetworkOptimizer/logs For remote access, use a properly configured HTTPS reverse proxy rather than exposing the HTTP interface directly to the Internet.

Source Code & Documentation

Official GitHub repository: https://github.com/Ozark-Connect/NetworkOptimizer Official documentation: https://github.com/Ozark-Connect/NetworkOptimizer/blob/main/README.md Original project developed by Ozark Connect. QNAP native packaging provides an alternative deployment method specifically adapted for QTS and QuTS hero environments.

items.name: UniFi Insights (Apache85) ( PostgreSQL17)
items.description:
Real-time UniFi Network Monitoring, Syslog Analytics & Threat Intelligence

UniFi Insights Plus is a powerful, self-hosted network monitoring and security analytics solution designed for UniFi gateways and routers. This QNAP edition runs natively on QTS 6 and QuTS hero 6, without Docker, combining a Python-based Syslog receiver, PostgreSQL database and a modern React web dashboard.

Key Features

  • Live Syslog Monitoring: Real-time firewall, DHCP, Wi-Fi, DNS and system event analysis.
  • Interactive Dashboard: Network statistics, traffic trends, blocked connections and device activity.
  • Threat Intelligence: IP reputation and security scoring through AbuseIPDB.
  • GeoIP & ASN: Geographic location, ISP identification and reverse DNS enrichment using MaxMind GeoLite2.
  • Threat Map: Interactive visualization of network threats.
  • Network Flow Analysis: Sankey diagrams, traffic direction detection and VLAN visibility.
  • UniFi Integration: Automatic network discovery, device identification and firewall Syslog management.
  • Multi-WAN & VPN: Support for multiple WAN interfaces and VPN connections.
  • Data Management: Configurable log retention, CSV export and configuration backup.
  • Responsive Interface: Modern dashboard with light and dark themes.
  • Persistent Storage: PostgreSQL data and user configuration are preserved during package upgrades.

Compatibility & Requirements

Supported systems: QTS 6 / QuTS hero 6 Architectures: x86_64 and ARM64 (aarch64) Required QPKG dependencies:
  • Apache85 — Python 3.12 runtime
  • PostgreSQL17 — Database engine
Recommended hardware: 4 CPU threads, 4 GB RAM and at least 10 GB of available storage. Actual requirements depend on Syslog traffic and retention settings. Docker and Container Station are not required.

Network Ports

  • 8090/TCP: Web dashboard and REST API
  • 514/UDP: UniFi Syslog receiver
  • 55432/TCP: Private PostgreSQL instance (localhost only)
Web and Syslog ports are configurable.

Quick Start

1. Install dependencies Install and enable Apache85 and PostgreSQL17 before installing UniFi Insights Plus. 2. Install and start UniFi Insights Plus Install the QPKG through QNAP App Center. The application initializes its private PostgreSQL database and creates its configuration automatically on the first successful startup. 3. Access the dashboard Open your browser and navigate to: http://YOUR-NAS-IP:8090 Follow the setup wizard to connect your UniFi controller using a UniFi OS API key or supported controller credentials. 4. Configure UniFi Syslog forwarding In UniFi Network 10.x: Navigate to Settings → Integrations → Syslog.
  • Enable Activity Logging.
  • Select SIEM Server.
  • Enter your QNAP NAS IP address.
  • Set the destination port to 514 UDP.
  • Enable Firewall Default Policy logging and other desired event categories.
Save the configuration. On older UniFi Network versions, configure remote Syslog forwarding through the corresponding system logging settings. 5. Configure optional integrations For enhanced analytics, configure:
  • MaxMind GeoLite2 account and license key for GeoIP/ASN database updates.
  • AbuseIPDB API key for IP reputation and threat scoring.
  • UniFi API access for automatic device and interface discovery.

Service Management

Start: /etc/init.d/Unifi-insight-plus.sh start Stop: /etc/init.d/Unifi-insight-plus.sh stop Restart: /etc/init.d/Unifi-insight-plus.sh restart Check status: /opt/Unifi-insight-plus/status.sh Health check: /opt/Unifi-insight-plus/healthcheck.sh

Configuration & Logs

Installation directory: /opt/Unifi-insight-plus Configuration: /opt/Unifi-insight-plus/config/unifi-insights-plus.env PostgreSQL data: /opt/Unifi-insight-plus/data/postgresql Logs: /opt/Unifi-insight-plus/logs Existing configuration files and PostgreSQL databases are preserved during package updates. Backups are recommended before major upgrades.

Security Notes

The dashboard uses HTTP by default. Keep access restricted to trusted networks or provide HTTPS through a properly configured reverse proxy. PostgreSQL is restricted to localhost and does not expose its database port to the network.

Project Information

Original developer: jmasarweh GitHub: https://github.com/jmasarweh/UniFi-Insights-Plus Documentation: https://insightsplus.dev/docs License: Business Source License 1.1 (BSL 1.1) QNAP integration: Community native QPKG adaptation, not an official QNAP or Ubiquiti package.

items.name: Media Preview Generator (QMultimedia-Q6)
items.description:
Media Preview Generator (MPG-Q6) is a media preview and thumbnail generation solution for QNAP NAS systems running QTS 6 or QuTS hero 6. It provides a web-based interface for managing media processing tasks, generating previews and thumbnails, and analyzing media files. MPG-Q6 integrates with QMultimedia-Q6, reusing its Python 3.13 environment, FFmpeg and FFprobe binaries to avoid unnecessary duplication of multimedia components.

Features

  • Modern web-based management interface
  • Media preview and thumbnail generation
  • Video and image processing
  • MediaInfo integration for detailed media metadata
  • FFmpeg and FFprobe integration through QMultimedia-Q6
  • Support for Intel/AMD x86_64 and ARM64 architectures
  • Automatic startup with the NAS
  • Dedicated start, stop, restart, status and health-check scripts
  • Authentication token for web interface access
  • Persistent configuration across package updates
  • Dedicated application logs
  • Integration with QTS App Center
Hardware acceleration, HDR processing and advanced media features depend on the capabilities of the NAS hardware, drivers and installed FFmpeg build.

Compatibility

Supported operating systems:
  • QNAP QTS 6.x
  • QNAP QuTS hero 6.x
Supported architectures:
  • x86_64 (Intel / AMD)
  • ARM64 (aarch64)
Required dependency:
  • QMultimedia-Q6, providing Python 3.13, FFmpeg and FFprobe
QMultimedia-Q6 must be installed and enabled before starting MPG-Q6.

Quick Start

1. Install QMultimedia-Q6

Download and install the latest compatible QMultimedia-Q6 package from myQNAP.org. Make sure the dependency is running correctly before proceeding.

2. Install MPG-Q6

Download the MPG-Q6 package matching your NAS architecture. Open QTS App Center → Install Manually, select the downloaded package and complete the installation.

3. Open the Web Interface

Launch MPG-Q6 from the QTS desktop or App Center. Alternatively, open the following address in your browser: http://NAS-IP:14578 Replace NAS-IP with your NAS IP address or hostname. Default web port: 14578/TCP

4. Retrieve Your Authentication Token

MPG-Q6 uses an authentication token to protect access to its management interface. To locate your token:
  1. Log in to your NAS administration interface.
  2. Open QuLog Center.
  3. Navigate to Event Logs / System Event Logs.
  4. Look for an event generated by MPG-Q6.
  5. Copy the authentication token displayed in the event details.
  6. Return to the MPG-Q6 login page and paste the token into the authentication field.
Important: Keep your authentication token confidential. Anyone possessing a valid token may be able to access the MPG-Q6 management interface. If the token is not visible in QuLog Center, check the application startup logs or verify that MPG-Q6 started successfully.

5. Configure the Application

After authentication, configure the available media processing options according to your requirements. Verify that your media directories are accessible and that the NAS has sufficient storage space for generated previews.

6. Start Processing

Use the web interface to configure and manage your media preview generation tasks. Processing performance depends on the NAS CPU, available memory, storage performance and FFmpeg capabilities.

Service Management

MPG-Q6 is installed under: /opt/MPG-Q6 The following commands can be executed through SSH. Start the application: /bin/sh /opt/MPG-Q6/start.sh Stop the application: /bin/sh /opt/MPG-Q6/stop.sh Restart the application: /bin/sh /opt/MPG-Q6/restart.sh Check application status: /bin/sh /opt/MPG-Q6/status.sh Run a health check: /bin/sh /opt/MPG-Q6/healthcheck.sh

Network Configuration

Default web interface: http://NAS-IP:14578 Default port: 14578/TCP Protocol: HTTP The web port can be customized through the package configuration. For remote access, a secure reverse proxy with HTTPS or a VPN is recommended. Avoid exposing the HTTP management interface directly to the public internet.

Logs and Troubleshooting

Application logs are stored in: /opt/MPG-Q6/logs/ If MPG-Q6 fails to start, inspect the startup and Gunicorn logs. Common checks include:
  • Verify that QMultimedia-Q6 is installed and running.
  • Confirm that Python 3.13, FFmpeg and FFprobe are available.
  • Ensure that TCP port 14578 is not already in use.
  • Check the application logs for startup or dependency errors.
  • Verify that the authentication token is available in QuLog Center.
  • Run the health-check script to diagnose service availability.
MPG-Q6 relies on compatible Python and OpenSSL libraries supplied by QMultimedia-Q6. Avoid overriding these libraries with incompatible third-party versions.

Updates and Configuration Persistence

MPG-Q6 is designed to preserve existing application configuration during package updates. For additional safety, back up your configuration before performing major upgrades. Keep MPG-Q6 and QMultimedia-Q6 updated to compatible versions.

Important Notes

MPG-Q6 is designed specifically for QNAP NAS systems running QTS 6 or QuTS hero 6. Advanced hardware acceleration depends on the NAS model, installed drivers and FFmpeg capabilities. MPG-Q6 is an independent community package and is not an official QNAP application.

items.name: Chromium Station (QMultimedia-Q6)
items.description:
Chromium Station provides isolated and persistent Chromium browser sessions directly on a QNAP NAS. It is designed for QTS 6.x and QuTS hero 6.x, with support for both x86_64 and ARM64 / aarch64 builds. Each virtual browser runs independently with its own persistent profile, cookies, sessions and settings. Chromium runs under the dedicated non-root chromiumsvc account with the Chromium sandbox enabled. The management service listens only on the NAS loopback interface and is exposed through the QTS application proxy. The ARM64 build is now native: the builder detects aarch64, compiles both Chromium Station binaries as ARM64 ELF files, and runs the full native test suite on that architecture. Chromium-build-v98-20261021T113…

Required dependencies

Chromium Station requires:
  • QTS 6.x or QuTS hero 6.x
  • QMultimedia-Q6
  • A supported QNAP NAS architecture:
    • x86_64
    • ARM64 / aarch64
  • A recent QNAP firmware with Linux user namespaces available for the Chromium sandbox
QMultimedia-Q6 is used as an optional runtime dependency source when a required compatible system library is not already bundled or available natively. No separate Node.js, Go, Python or browser package is required on the NAS itself. The Chromium runtime, fonts, Fontconfig, GSettings and NSS components needed by the package are prepared and bundled by the build process.

Main features

  • Multiple independent Chromium browser profiles
  • Persistent browser sessions and cookies
  • Native x86_64 and ARM64 support
  • Dedicated non-root Chromium account
  • Chromium sandbox enabled
  • Interactive browser view directly inside QTS
  • Back, Forward and Reload controls
  • Address bar navigation
  • Mouse, keyboard, scroll and double-click support
  • Copy, cut and paste between the local computer and virtual browser
  • Automatic proportional scaling
  • Selectable browser resolutions
  • Browser zoom controls
  • Adaptive refresh rate and image quality
  • Live latency indication
  • Automatic DevTools reconnection
  • Browser previews
  • Runtime and diagnostic logs
  • Downloadable diagnostic reports
  • 20 interface languages
  • QTS / QuTS hero integration
  • QTS proxy / CloudLink-compatible access
  • Persistent profiles across package restarts and upgrades
Quick Start
  1. Install and start QMultimedia-Q6.
  2. Install the Chromium Station QPKG from QTS App Center using Install Manually.
  3. Start Chromium Station from the QTS desktop.
  4. Open the Chromium Station interface and use Recheck Browser Engine.
  5. Verify that the browser engine is reported as available.
  6. Click Create Browser.
  7. Enter a browser name and initial URL, for example https://www.google.com
  8. Click Start.
  9. Click Live to open the interactive browser session.
Keyboard shortcuts Ctrl/Cmd + C — Copy Ctrl/Cmd + X — Cut Ctrl/Cmd + V — Paste Ctrl + L — Focus navigation Ctrl + R or F5 — Reload Alt + Left — Back Alt + Right — Forward Ctrl/Cmd + + — Zoom in Ctrl/Cmd + - — Zoom out Ctrl/Cmd + 0 — Reset zoom Thanks to report bugs into Discord Channel
